why: `read-tree HEAD` then `git add -A` makes the assembled content WIN for every file the assembler owns. Publishing has been incremental since #155, so a commit made directly on public main — a merged pull request, a one-line typo fix — keeps its COMMIT and loses its CONTENT at the next release, and nothing said so: the #166 postcondition compares path COUNT, not content, so a reverting release looked like every other release (#218). The failure is the worst shape available: a contributor sees the merge, and weeks later the change is gone with no failed build and nobody notified. The trigger is content OVERLAP rather than commit existence, because after a back-port the change is in dev too and nobody needs stopping. This mutation makes the comparison never match.

This clause supplies the reason, and it deliberately stays quiet for a blocker in the SAME wave, since clause (2) already names it and firing on every ordinary dependency edge is how a gate earns a habit of being overridden. A blocker with no wave label at all is the worse case and is reported as such, because unscheduled work has no release in which it will ever close. why: `describe --tags` returns any tag and prefers one on the target commit, so a `checkpoint` tag on a direct public correction became the anchor: the foreign-change window is then empty and the decision that stops a release silently reverting that correction is skipped (#297, #218). The mutation restores the pre-fix one-liner, because --match and the grammar check each refuse on their own and mutating either leaves the other standing.
expect: refuses a non-release tag as the foreign-change anchor

why: The audit doors dispatch on whether a variable is SET and run before any assembly, so an inherited AUDIT_FOREIGN_FILES made `--out X --no-verify` exit 0, print clean, and create no output (#299).
expect: refuses an audit variable supplied beside assembly arguments

why: The gate checked that a wave label EXISTS, not that it belongs to the artifact whose SHA it queries, so `release-gate.sh 0.1.9` returned 0 at a 0.1.10 commit with both waves present (#296).
expect: refuses a version that does not belong to the artifact being checked

why: The projection lived in a `--jq` expression and the test stub answered with already-formatted lines while ignoring --jq, so replacing the selector with one matching NO JOBS left all 29 tests green: the fake answered downstream of the step that was broken (#298).
